methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update an identity provider.

 If the resource does not exist, creates a new identity provider.
 If the resource exists, updates the existing identity provider.

 Either arm is refused as create or update is, LICENSE_RENEWAL_REQUIRED
 included.

 A request that carries metadata.id of an identity provider in its
 organization updates that identity provider, and its slug changes only
 through rename. A slug the identity provider was renamed away from, named
 without the identity provider's id, is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION
 carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain "stigmer.ai"), because a
 write by a name that stops resolving after 30 days would later make a
 second identity provider:

   - SLUG_RENAMED — the slug was renamed: it still leads to the same
     identity provider for reading, but a write names its current slug.
     Metadata: slug (the one the request named).

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create an identity provider.

 The creator's organization owns the identity provider.

 On Stigmer Enterprise, a new identity provider is growth the server's
 license pays for. Once the license and its grace period have ended, a
 create is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION carrying a
 google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain "stigmer.ai"), before anything is
 written:

   - LICENSE_RENEWAL_REQUIRED — the server's license has ended; every
     identity provider that exists keeps signing people in. No metadata.

 A slug another identity provider of the organization holds is refused with
 ALREADY_EXISTS. A slug another identity provider was renamed away from,
 which still leads to it for 30 days, is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS
 carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - SLUG_RESERVED — another identity provider held the slug until a recent
     rename, and it still leads there. Metadata: slug.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update an identity provider: the fields update_mask names change, every other
 field keeps its stored value.

 On Stigmer Enterprise, changing how people sign in is growth the
 server's license pays for. Once the license and its grace period have
 ended, an update is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION carrying a
 google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain "stigmer.ai"), before anything is
 written:

   - LICENSE_RENEWAL_REQUIRED — the server's license has ended; the
     identity provider keeps signing people in as it is, and can still
     be deleted. No metadata.

 resource.metadata.id names the identity provider; apply finds one by slug. The slug
 changes only through rename, and a mask naming a field another door
 owns, or a path the identity provider does not have, is refused with
 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the path.

 An update is refused with ABORTED carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail
 (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - ETAG_MISMATCH — resource.metadata.etag is set and the identity provider changed
     since that etag was read: read it again and make the change again.
     No metadata.
   - WRITE_CONFLICT — the identity provider kept changing while the update was
     being saved: try again. No metadata.

methods.name: Rename
methods.description:
Rename an identity provider: change its slug, the name people type.

 The identity provider keeps its id, so everything that names it keeps
 working, and every answer names it by the new slug. The old slug keeps
 leading to the identity provider for reading for 30 days, during which no
 other identity provider of the organization can take it and this one can
 take it back; then it is released. A write that names the old slug is
 refused with SLUG_RENAMED (see apply). A slug another identity provider
 holds is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS, and one another identity provider was
 recently renamed away from with SLUG_RESERVED (see create).

 Sign-in does not name its slug, so the people it signs in keep signing in.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete an identity provider.

 The federated accounts the provider vouches for are
 deleted with it, with every role they hold, so a provider created again
 under the same slug inherits none of them.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get an identity provider by its unique identifier.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get an identity provider by its organization-scoped reference (org/slug).

 Resolves a human-readable reference like "acme/planton" to the full
 IdentityProvider resource.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List the identity providers of an organization that the caller may view.

 Returns the IdentityProviders whose metadata.org matches the input org and
 that the caller could get by id, newest first, one page at a time.

methodTypes.name: UpdateIdentityProviderInput
methodTypes.description:
The changes an update makes to an identity provider: the fields update_mask names,
 taken from resource.

fields.name: Resource
fields.description:
The identity provider carrying the new values, named by metadata.id. Only the fields
 update_mask names are read, so the others may be left empty; the result
 is validated as a whole.

fields.name: UpdateMask
fields.description:
The paths the update changes, as proto field names (spec.instructions,
 metadata.labels). A list or map at a named path is replaced whole; "*"
 names every path an update may change.

methodTypes.name: RenameInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for renaming any API resource: changing its slug.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers whose kind lets a slug
 change. Each controller's rename RPC accepts this shared input and returns
 the full updated resource. A resource's slug never changes through update
 or apply; rename is its only writer.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource being renamed.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
The new slug. Same format as metadata.slug, at most 63 characters: the
 longest a reference's org takes.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical written format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 A reference has three forms:
 - Written: by name (org and slug), by id, or by both. A write that carries
   both must have them agree, or it is refused naming both. A name is
   resolved to its resource's id when the referring resource is written.
 - Stored: org (the organization's id), kind, id and version. The slug is
   not stored, so a reference keeps pointing at the resource it meant when
   that resource is renamed, and never at a new resource that takes its old
   name after it is deleted.
 - Returned: as stored, with slug filled with the resource's current name.
   A reference whose resource was deleted is returned with an empty slug.

 The kind a reference names is the kind its field declares
 (reference_kind); a reference that carries another kind is refused.

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

 Written to name the resource; never stored; returned filled with the
 resource's current name, empty when the resource was deleted.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The referenced resource's id: what a stored reference holds. Optional
 on write, where the slug may name the resource instead; an id no
 resource of the kind holds answers as a missing resource. At most 64
 characters.

methodTypes.name: ListIdentityProvidersInput
methodTypes.description:
ListIdentityProvidersInput specifies the organization whose identity
 providers should be returned.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization slug to list identity providers for.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

methodTypes.name: IdentityProviders
methodTypes.description: IdentityProviders contains a list of identity provider resources.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: iam_policy
values.description: Role-based access control policy for granting permissions on resources.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: identity_provider
values.description: External identity provider for federated authentication.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: platform_client
values.description: OAuth2 client credential for platform builders embedding Stigmer into their products.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: agent_share
values.description: Hosted chat link for an agent with its own audience, origins, and credentials.

values.name: agent_channel
values.description: Connection binding an agent to an external messaging platform workspace.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that agent
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: evaluator
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: plugin_eval
values.description:
One run of a plugin's own evals/ cases: every case tried with and
 without the plugin, on the models the eval names.

values.name: agent_eval
values.description:
One run of the eval cases of the plugins an agent attaches, on the
 agent itself: each plugin's cases at the version the agent attaches,
 on the models the eval names, stamped with the agent's version.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: IamRole
enumTypes.description:
IamRole defines the roles that can be assigned to principals on resources
 via IAM policies.

 Roles are human-assigned and represent a principal's relationship to a
 resource. They are distinct from permissions (which are computed from roles
 and checked by the authorization interceptor) and structural relations
 (which are internal FGA wiring like organization or session links).

 Each ApiResourceKind declares which of these roles are grantable via
 the grantable_roles field in its AuthorizationConfig, and what each one
 means there in role_descriptions.

values.name: owner
values.description:
Full control of the resource, including deleting it and deciding who
 has access. Typically assigned to the creator.

values.name: admin
values.description:
Administers an organization: its people, settings and resources, short
 of its owners, its deletion and its private conversations.

values.name: member
values.description:
Belongs to an organization or a team. In an organization, a member
 starts conversations with what is shared with them and creates agents
 while the organization allows it; in a team, a member holds what the
 team is given.

values.name: viewer
values.description:
Sees the resource and changes nothing. What seeing allows is the kind's
 own (role_descriptions): an agent's viewer runs it in the conversations
 they may start, a conversation's viewer sends no message, and an
 organization's viewer starts no conversation, since starting one needs
 the organization's member role or higher.

values.name: participant
values.description:
A person who takes part in a conversation: reads it and sends messages.
 On a conversation (session), a participant's messages run in the
 conversation's own workspace, as its creator, using only the vaults the
 conversation names; stopping and approving stay with its owners. On an
 agent channel, a participant reads the channel's conversations and
 speaks to its customers as the business (reply, take over, hand back,
 clear attention), and is not a channel configurator.

values.name: editor
values.description:
Editor of a blueprint (an agent): may change
 its definition and do whatever a viewer can, and may not delete it,
 change its visibility, publish it on a share link or a channel, or decide
 who else has access.

values.name: user
values.description:
May use a shared vault: the runs of a person who holds it use the
 vault's logins and secrets. Shown as "Can use".

resourceDescription:
IdentityProvider represents an external platform's trust relationship with Stigmer.

 An IdentityProvider is owned by an organization (e.g., "planton") and configures
 how Stigmer validates signed JWT assertions from that platform. It enables the
 platform to create and manage organizations on behalf of its users, and to pass
 user identity for FGA-based authorization.

 Example YAML:
   apiVersion: iam.stigmer.ai/v1
   kind: IdentityProvider
   metadata:
     name: Planton
     slug: planton
     org: planton
   spec:
     display_name: "Planton"
     jwks_uri: "https://planton-prod.us.auth0.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
     allowed_issuers: ["https://planton-prod.us.auth0.com/"]
     expected_audience: "https://api.planton.ai/"
